label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
To: reviews/arroyo-precision-works
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Fast, careful, and they actually read the drawing. 5/5

Our group (Ostrowski lab, Astronomy) ordered two parts from Arroyo for our near-IR camera: a camera-to-dewar adapter plate and a light baffle tube with internal threads. Both are 6061-T6 with black anodize. We needed them for our Palomar 200-inch run on Nov 18, so the schedule was tight. I want to give the details because I think other labs and purchasing will find them more useful than just "great shop".

**Lead time**
Arroyo quoted 21 days. The parts arrived 9 days after the PO, including the anodize. For comparison, one of the big vendors quoted us 6 weeks for the same parts, which would have missed our telescope run completely. Our total was $2,840, including a $300 rush setup fee. For two custom anodized parts on this timeline I think that is very fair.

**They read the drawing (and caught my mistake)**
I have to admit this part was my fault. On sheet 2 of the plate drawing, I wrote the bolt circle as 4.125. Every other dimension on the drawing is in mm. I copied that number from an old drawing for our previous camera and never converted it. It should have been 4.125 inch (104.8 mm). Tiff at Arroyo noticed it while setting up the job. She saw that at 4.125 mm the screws would land inside the bore. Ruben emailed me to confirm before they cut anything.

If they had just machined what was on the paper, we would have had a useless plate a week before the run, with no time to remake it. A lot of shops cut exactly what you send them, and that is technically correct. Arroyo actually looked at whether the part made sense. For research hardware, where our drawings are not always perfect (mine clearly wasn't), this matters a lot.

**Quality (from our fit test on Monday)**
- Adapter plate onto the dewar: all 8 screws went in with no forcing.
- Flatness across the face was < 0.01 mm on the dial indicator.
- Baffle threads were smooth.
- Dark test with the lab lights on and a 300 s dark frame showed no light leak. The result was the same as with the dewar closed. For an IR camera this is the test that really counts.
- The anodize is even, with no bare spots.
- They also included an inspection sheet with the parts.

Everything worked the first time, which almost never happens for us.

**Communication and service**
Ruben answered questions quickly once the job started, and he kept me updated. When the parts were done, he drove them to the Robinson loading dock himself on his way to another supplier, and he did not charge for delivery. Honestly, I was so happy I almost hugged him. That kind of thing means a lot when you have a telescope deadline.

**For purchasing**
I would really like Arroyo to be added to the preferred vendor list. Our group would use them again, and I think other labs doing instrument work should know about them. They are a small shop, but they were faster than the big vendor, cheaper than paying for a remake, and much more careful. Their material list (aluminum, stainless, Invar, PEEK) also covers most of what we use for optics and cryo mounts.

One small note to be fair: another review mentioned slow quotes, and our quote also took a little longer than I expected to arrive. Once we had the quote, though, everything moved very fast. If your timeline is tight, just ask early.

5/5 from me. Thank you Ruben and Tiff!

Lin Wei, Postdoc, Ostrowski group (Astronomy)
